question.text: Which of the following indices uses a price-weighted methodology?

answer.text: Dow Jones Industrial Average and Nikkei 225

explanation.text: The Logic: The Series VIII workbook (page 21) names the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the Nikkei 225 as popular examples of price-weighted indices. In a price-weighted index, stocks with higher share prices have a greater influence on the index, regardless of the company's total market capitalisation. The Trap: Sensex and Nifty 50 are well known Indian benchmarks but use free-float market-capitalisation weighting, not price weighting. Other distractors mix global and sectoral indices to test whether the candidate has the price-weighted examples specifically supported by the workbook. Note: Remembering the two flagship price-weighted indices — DJIA and Nikkei 225 — is the fastest way to answer methodology questions of this type.
